_provenance.syllabus: marks, AOs, lengths, texts and the three categories: syllabus pages 19-21
_provenance.corpus: the AO split inside each question and the level ladders: the 68 published AS mark schemes, 2021-2025; every ladder appears with the same bands in all 34 schemes for its paper
_provenance.derivation_policy: The level descriptors are paraphrased in our words. No mark-scheme wording is to reach learner-facing output; paraphrase again when teaching them.

9093.subject: Cambridge International AS Level English Language

P1-Q1a.name: Question 1(a), directed response
P1-Q1a.text: one unseen text of about 550–750 words
P1-Q1a.provenance: syllabus, page 19 (the task, the lengths, AO1 and AO2); the 5 + 5 split is corpus, from the mark schemes
P1-Q1a.set_as: a new form for a named audience and purpose, re-using the source’s content (corpus). Forms set in the 34 papers: email 6, speech 5, letter 4, advertisement 4, diary 4, report 3, blog 2, podcast 2, leaflet 2, brochure 1, review 1. A role is given in 24 of the 34.
P1-Q1a.word_range_rule: no fixed deduction for the count; an answer well outside the range is marked as a poorer fit to the form and purpose (corpus, every scheme)

levels.requires: a subtle, assured grasp of the source’s meaning, context and audience; its typical features drawn on perceptively
a thorough grasp of the source’s meaning, context and audience; its typical features drawn on well
a secure grasp of meaning, context and audience; its typical features drawn on plainly
a partial grasp of meaning, context and audience; little use of its typical features
a slight grasp of the source; almost no use of its typical features
assured, highly accurate writing; everything suits the audience and purpose, and ideas are developed with subtlety from start to finish
effective writing with only small slips that never obscure meaning; content suits the audience and purpose, ideas developed well
clear writing with occasional slips; content suits the audience and purpose, ideas developed plainly
clear but uneven writing, with frequent slips that mostly leave meaning intact; content mostly suits the task, thin development
basic writing whose errors often obscure meaning; content may drift from the audience and purpose, almost no development

P1-Q1b.name: Question 1(b), comparison
P1-Q1b.text: the Question 1(a) source and the candidate’s own response
P1-Q1b.provenance: syllabus, page 19 (the task, AO1 and AO3); the 5 + 10 split is corpus, from the mark schemes
P1-Q1b.set_as: the instruction opens with Compare and names form, structure and language in all 34 papers (corpus)
P1-Q1b.organisation_rule: form, structure and language need not be taken in separate sections (corpus, every scheme)

levels.requires: a subtle comparative grasp of both texts’ meaning, context and audience; typical features drawn on perceptively
a thorough comparative grasp of both texts; typical features drawn on well
a secure comparative grasp of both texts; typical features drawn on plainly
a partial grasp of the texts with little comparison; little use of typical features
a slight grasp of the texts with almost no comparison; almost no use of typical features
a subtle, assured comparison of form, structure and language across both texts, explaining with precision how each writer’s choices suit its audience and create meaning
a detailed comparison of form, structure and language across both texts, and of how the choices suit each audience and create meaning
a clear comparison of form, structure or language across the texts, and of how the choices suit audience and meaning
some analysis of form, structure or language but little comparison; choices only loosely tied to audience and meaning
very little analysis or comparison; choices hardly tied to audience or meaning

P1-Q2.name: Question 2, text analysis
P1-Q2.text: one unseen text of about 550–750 words
P1-Q2.provenance: syllabus, page 20 (the task, AO1 and AO3); the 5 + 20 split is corpus, from the mark schemes
P1-Q2.set_as: Analyse, focusing on form, structure and language, in all 34 papers (corpus). Sources: newspaper or magazine article 11, fiction or narrative 5, blog or website 4, memoir, autobiography or diary 3, speech, talk or podcast transcript 3, review 2, travel writing 2, other 2, advertisement, leaflet or brochure 1, letter or email 1

levels.requires: a subtle, assured grasp of the text’s meaning, context and audience; its typical features drawn on perceptively
a thorough grasp of meaning, context and audience; its typical features drawn on well
a secure grasp of meaning, context and audience; its typical features drawn on plainly
a partial grasp of meaning, context and audience; little use of its typical features
a slight grasp of the text; almost no use of its typical features

an assured, coherent analysis that is very well organised; features chosen with insight; a subtle sense of how the writer’s choices suit the audience and make meaning; exact, apt language joining evidence to comment
a detailed, coherent, well-organised analysis; well-chosen features; a detailed sense of how the choices suit the audience and make meaning; effective language joining evidence to comment
a clear, coherent analysis with a sound structure; suitable features chosen; a clear sense of how the choices suit the audience and make meaning; clear language joining evidence to comment
some structure but limited coherence; some suitable features chosen; a limited sense of the writer’s choices; an attempt to join evidence to comment
a basic analysis with little structure; few features chosen; little sense of the writer’s choices; evidence and comment barely joined

P2-Q1a.name: Question 1(a), shorter writing
P2-Q1a.set_as: a form for a named audience and purpose; in 29 of the 34 papers the prompt adds a focus sentence (corpus). Forms: speech 7, email 6, story 5, blog 5, report 3, leaflet 3, letter 2, diary 2
P2-Q1a.marking_rules: expression and accuracy count equally with development and organisation; each strand counts equally inside a level; the word limit is judged as part of task achievement, not by deduction (corpus, every scheme)

levels.requires: assured expression drawing on a broad repertoire of structures and vocabulary, some complex or unusual; very few errors; organised with clear logic and strong effect, ideas developed with subtlety throughout; the task achieved in full, everything relevant; the audience held throughout

effective expression using a range of structures and vocabulary, some complex or unusual; a few small slips that never obscure meaning; logically organised, ideas developed effectively; the task well achieved, content relevant; the audience engaged

clear expression with some complex structures and some unusual vocabulary, perhaps with repetition; occasional slips that do not obscure meaning; clearly organised, ideas developed clearly; the task achieved, content relevant; the audience addressed

clear expression that may not flow, in mostly common structures and vocabulary; frequent slips that mostly leave meaning intact; some organisation, thin development; the task broadly achieved, content mostly relevant; little sense of the audience

basic expression in mostly simple structures and common words; errors that obscure meaning; little organisation or development; the task misread or only partly done, some content irrelevant; almost no sense of the audience
assured analysis of the text’s form, structure and language, and of how the choices suit its audience and shape its meaning
detailed analysis of form, structure and language, and of how the choices suit the audience and shape meaning
clear analysis of form, structure and language, and of how the choices suit the audience and shape meaning
limited analysis of form, structure or language, and of how the choices suit the audience
minimal analysis of form, structure or language, and of how the choices suit the audience

P2-B.name: Section B, extended writing
P2-B.choice: one question from three, one per category: imaginative/descriptive, discursive/argumentative, review/critical
P2-B.set_as: one question per category in all 34 papers, in six different orders, so a question number never identifies a category; imaginative/descriptive: narrative 19, descriptive 15, a focus added in 33, a given sentence in 9; discursive/argumentative: article 14, essay 12, speech 8, letter 4; review/critical: a review in all 34 (corpus)

levels.requires: assured expression drawing on a broad repertoire of structures and vocabulary, some complex or unusual; very few errors; organised with clear logic and strong effect, ideas developed with subtlety throughout; the task achieved in full, everything relevant; the audience held throughout

effective expression using a range of structures and vocabulary, some complex or unusual; a few small slips that never obscure meaning; logically organised, ideas developed effectively; the task well achieved, content relevant; the audience engaged

clear expression with some complex structures and some unusual vocabulary, perhaps with repetition; occasional slips that do not obscure meaning; clearly organised, ideas developed clearly; the task achieved, content relevant; the audience addressed

clear expression that may not flow, in mostly common structures and vocabulary; frequent slips that mostly leave meaning intact; some organisation, thin development; the task broadly achieved, content mostly relevant; little sense of the audience

basic expression in mostly simple structures and common words; errors that obscure meaning; little organisation or development; the task misread or only partly done, some content irrelevant; almost no sense of the audience
